evidence.mission_note: A 987.2 manual Boxster S fits the enthusiast brief and resale goals well. At $39,500 it sits well outside the bridge budget ($27,000 max price), so it reads more like a keeper-class purchase than a bridge.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a 2012 987.2 Boxster S with a VIN that decodes consistently (3.4L, convertible), a 6-speed manual and Sport Chrono visible in photos, and a Black Edition sill plate. The seller itemises recent work with mileages at a named Porsche specialist: 40k service, clutch at 39,800, power steering lines, battery and oil service at 43,000. No invoices or history report were captured. Observed issues are the seller-disclosed rear tires at 3/32 and an early clutch replacement whose cause is unexplained, which makes an over-rev report important. The 9A1 engine removes the IMS question, but nothing documents cooling-system components on a 14-year-old car, and seat-belt recall 11V409000 completion is unknown. The $39,500 asking price exceeds both the computed fair-value band (which is drawn from 987.1 comps and understates a 987.2 Black Edition) and the stated $27,000 max price. Photos show a clean, straight car, but the underside and top drains are not examined here.
evidence.next_action: Ask the seller for the RMG invoices (especially the clutch job), tire date codes and recall status, and whether he will permit a PIWIS-backed PPI in the Bay Area, and gauge his flexibility on the $39,500 asking price before spending more time.
